newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Savoy Hotel, executives reported for unfair trade.
newsitem.headline: Savoy Hotel, executives reported for unfair trade.

text.p: South Korea's Securities Supervisory Board said on Tuesday it had reported Savoy Hotel and five executives to prosecutors for alleged violations of stock trading rules.

The board said in a statement Savoy Hotel, Savoy Construction, five hotel executives, including president, and two others close to Savoy had been accused of secretly buying shares of New Star Trading.
They raised their combined stake in New Star to 41.43 percent by buying 41,830 shares April 11 to 25. "The purchase should have been made in the open market," it said.

The statement also said Savoy Hotel and Savoy Construction were accused of deliberately deleting a 16.7 percent stake held by two close associates of Savoy in applications to take over New Star, which were submitted to the board in April and May.
Separately, the president of Woongjin Corway, a water purifier maker, was also reported to prosecutors for not reporting the April sale of his 9.63 percent stake in New Star.

An SSB official said the board ordered those on Savoy's side to reduce its holding in New Star to 24.7 percent by August 27. The board also suspended the Savoy group's purchase of New Star shares in the open market.
In another case, the SSB reported to prosecutors insider trading by three executives of Ilyang Pharmaceutical.
The three were suspected of buying Ilyang shares before announcing the company's plan for rights and bonus issues in May 1996.
